also: cheat someone out of his money

terms.comment: With the accusative of the person and the ablative of what he is cheated of: aliquem argentō fraudāre, to cheat someone out of his money.

terms.gloss: swindle someone out of his money
evidence: Ter. Ph. 4.4.1: ēmūnxī argentō senēs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Literally “to wipe someone’s nose”; in comedy, to fleece him (Lewis & Short).

phrases.english: to cheat someone out of his money

sources: Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 289, 290.
